recommendations.regimenLabel: Treat the cause + blood-product support (guided by bleeding and levels)
steps: TREAT THE UNDERLYING CAUSE — this is the priority (sepsis, obstetric emergency, malignancy).
Bleeding/high-risk: replace with platelets, fresh frozen plasma, and cryoprecipitate/fibrinogen guided by levels.
Thrombotic phenotype without bleeding: consider therapeutic anticoagulation (specialist-guided).

drugRefs.regimenLabel: FFP for prolonged PT/APTT with bleeding
drugRefs.freq: guided by repeat PT/APTT and bleeding
drugRefs.why: Replaces consumed clotting factors in the bleeding patient with prolonged PT/APTT.

drugRefs.dose: 1 adult dose (pool); target >50 ×10⁹/L in active bleeding
drugRefs.why: Corrects consumptive thrombocytopenia in the bleeding or high-bleeding-risk patient.
Replaces fibrinogen when depleted by consumption; alternative is fibrinogen concentrate.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Coagulation Disorders (Ch. 121)
ISTH Guidance for Diagnosis and Management of DIC
BSH Guideline on the Diagnosis and Management of DIC

drugRefs.dose: weight-based IV infusion titrated to APTT (specialist-directed)
drugRefs.why: Considered only in a predominantly thrombotic phenotype without active bleeding; started under haematology guidance.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Coagulation Disorders (Ch. 121)
ISTH Guidance for Diagnosis and Management of DIC

confirm: Bleeding and/or thrombosis with consumptive coagulopathy (low platelets, high PT/APTT, low fibrinogen, high D-dimer) secondary to a trigger (sepsis, malignancy, obstetric).
